_comment: Rejected English renderings, per FR term. glossary.json says what a term SHOULD be; this file says what it currently is where it is wrong, which is campaign state, not a permanent property of the terminology. `to` is cross-checked against the glossary entry's `en` at load time. Mechanical rules only fire when the aligned FRENCH block matches `fr_regex`; spelling rules are English orthography and carry no FR gate.

rules.note: «section unité» and «élément unité» are legitimately unit section / unit element and are not matched by this rule
vetoed when the French quotes it: « partie finie » names the finite component of a decomposition (sga3 X-4#11), like «partie unipotente» → unipotent part, and is not a subset
"flabby" is in the entry's en_accept — accepted for reading, but the corpus keeps the French word, so the 5 stray occurrences are normalized

spelling.note: British spelling is the house form (glossary «fibre»). Bibliography blocks are skipped — English paper titles keep their own spelling (sga6 II-bibliographie cites Shih, «Fiber cobordism…»).
Closed-up spelling is the house form (glossary «sous-groupe» → subgroup, «sous-schéma en groupes» → subgroup scheme); sga3 IX/XVII and sga7 exposé 9 print the hyphenated form.

judgment.reason: «H majore K» is "H contains K" in a subgroup/subscheme-inclusion context; elsewhere bound / upper bound
scheme-theoretic «X au-dessus de S» is "X over S"; "above" is correct only in its ordinary spatial/textual sense
the sheaf-at-a-point sense is "stalk", the topos/Galois sense is "fibre" — fixes exist in both directions, never scripted
«ce numéro» is the numbered section of the exposé, not an article
